questions.question: An Azure Function must run only when a file with the .pdf extension is created in the contracts container of a storage account. Other files and other containers must not invoke the function. What should you configure on the Event Grid event subscription?

options.text: Filter on the Microsoft.Storage.BlobCreated event type, with subject begins with set to the contracts container path and subject ends with set to .pdf
options.why: Correct. Event type and subject filters limit delivery to new PDF blobs in the contracts container.

options.text: Set the maximum delivery attempts to 1
options.why: This changes the retry policy. It does not filter which events are delivered.

options.text: Configure a dead-letter destination
options.why: Dead-lettering stores undeliverable events. It does not filter events.

options.text: Change the topic input schema to CloudEvents 1.0
options.why: The schema defines the event format. It does not restrict which events reach the handler.

questions.explanation: Event subscriptions support event type filters and subject begins with and ends with filters. Blob subjects include the container name and the blob name.

questions.question: An event subscription uses the default retry policy. The webhook handler is unavailable. Which statement describes how Azure Event Grid behaves?

options.text: Event Grid retries with exponential backoff for up to 30 attempts or 1,440 minutes, whichever limit is reached first
options.why: Correct. These are the default maximum delivery attempts and event time to live.

options.text: Event Grid retries every second indefinitely until the handler responds
options.why: Retries use exponential backoff and stop at the configured limits.

options.text: Event Grid stores the event in the topic until the handler pulls it
options.why: Push delivery to a webhook does not wait for the handler to pull events.

options.text: Event Grid moves the event to a Service Bus dead-letter queue after 10 attempts
options.why: Event Grid dead-letters to a storage blob container, and the default attempt limit is 30.

questions.explanation: Both the maximum delivery attempts (1 to 30) and the event time to live (1 to 1,440 minutes) can be lowered on the event subscription.

questions.scenario: A custom topic delivers events to a webhook. Events that cannot be delivered after all retry attempts must be retained for later analysis.
questions.question: What should you configure?

options.text: A dead-letter destination that points to a blob container in an Azure Storage account
options.why: Correct. Event Grid writes undelivered events to the dead-letter blob container.

options.text: A higher event time to live of 7 days
options.why: The event time to live cannot exceed 1,440 minutes, and retrying longer does not retain events that still fail.

options.text: An advanced filter on the data field
options.why: Advanced filters select events for delivery. They do not retain failed events.

options.text: Duplicate detection on the custom topic
options.why: Event Grid topics do not provide duplicate detection, and it would not retain failed events.

questions.explanation: Without a dead-letter destination, Event Grid drops events after the retry policy is exhausted.

questions.question: A Python application must publish custom events to an Event Grid custom topic that uses the CloudEvents 1.0 input schema. The application authenticates by using Microsoft Entra ID. Which code should you use?

options.text: EventGridPublisherClient(endpoint, DefaultAzureCredential()).send([CloudEvent(source=..., type=..., data=...)])
options.why: Correct. EventGridPublisherClient sends CloudEvent objects, and DefaultAzureCredential uses Microsoft Entra ID.

options.text: ServiceBusClient(endpoint, DefaultAzureCredential()).get_queue_sender(...)
options.why: ServiceBusClient sends messages to Service Bus, not events to Event Grid.

options.text: EventGridPublisherClient(endpoint, DefaultAzureCredential()).send([EventGridEvent(...)])
options.why: EventGridEvent uses the Event Grid schema. The topic expects the CloudEvents 1.0 schema.

options.text: BlobServiceClient(endpoint, DefaultAzureCredential()).upload_blob(...)
options.why: Uploading a blob raises a system event from Storage. It does not publish to the custom topic.

questions.explanation: Publish events in the schema that the topic was created with. The identity also needs the EventGrid Data Sender role on the topic.

questions.question: You create an Event Grid subscription that delivers events in the Event Grid schema to a custom HTTPS endpoint. The subscription remains in a failed state and no events are received. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The endpoint did not return the validationCode as validationResponse for the subscription validation event
options.why: Correct. A webhook must complete the validation handshake before Event Grid delivers events.

options.text: The topic does not have a dead-letter destination
options.why: Dead-lettering is optional and does not prevent the subscription from being created.

options.text: The maximum delivery attempts value is set to 30
options.why: 30 is the default value and does not prevent delivery.

options.text: The endpoint uses HTTPS
options.why: Event Grid webhooks are expected to use HTTPS.

questions.explanation: Event Grid sends a SubscriptionValidationEvent. The endpoint must echo the code or the validation URL must be opened. Azure Functions Event Grid triggers handle this automatically.
